claims.text: The proposed material system is AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock.
Machine-learning-based optimization of process conditions is applicable to additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Machine learning can optimize additive-manufacturing process conditions.
Laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing are the process parameters to be optimized.
Joint optimization of alloy composition and process parameters can minimize additive-manufacturing defects.
Joint optimization of alloy composition and process parameters can enhance manufacturing reliability.
Machine-learning optimization will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Machine-learning optimization will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Machine-learning optimization will increase processing efficiency relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The applicability boundary is additive manufacturing of miniature components from AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions constitute the comparison baseline.
The magnitude of the predicted mechanical-property and residual-stress improvements is unknown and requires experimental validation.
A controlled comparison can evaluate mechanical properties, residual thermal stresses, and processing efficiency under optimized and conventional conditions.
Failure to obtain significant improvement in mechanical properties, residual-stress reduction, and processing efficiency would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is defined as optimization of process conditions for a fixed AlCrFeNiSi feedstock, but the stated mechanism additionally requires optimization of alloy composition. Composition optimization is therefore outside the declared intervention and boundary.
